diagnosis: The lone decision-maker was able to satisfy checks C1, C3, and C6 without access to PF1 and PF2 because the decisions made were aligned with default settings or easily achievable thresholds. For example, seeking a narrow protective order and limiting the discovery scope to relevant and non-intrusive areas are common strategies that do not require specific private facts. Check C6, which depends on PF2, was satisfied due to the default setting of client retention at $75,000, as the value of 50,000 USD was within a reasonable range.

C1.why: The forensic count changes the response from broad inspection to a protective order covering exactly three files, and the absence of customer data changes customer-data production from required to prohibited.

C3.why: The forensic count changes the response from broad inspection to a protective order covering exactly three files, and the absence of customer data changes customer-data production from required to prohibited.

C6.why: The policy endorsement changes counsel selection to insurer-approved panel counsel, sets the client retention at exactly $75,000, requires written insurer consent for forensic work, and makes insurer notification part of the approved plan.
